narrative_prose: Hector gritted his teeth, the taste of ozone and oxidized iron thick on his tongue as the storm raged around him. The dark, metallic waves of the ferrofluid sea rose like iron fangs against the shoreline, defying gravity as the Kelvin-Helmholtz shear violently contorted their surface. Overhead, the sky bled an angry violet, illuminating the jagged basalt spires that stood as silent sentinels. Each gust of wind carried the terrifying hum of sheer magnetic force tearing through the atmosphere. He could feel the static charge making the hairs on his arm stand up, accompanied by an eerie, sudden chill. He needed to secure the rig before the shear intensified. Spotting Kaio scrambling up the ridge below, pockets bulging with glowing moss, Hector calculated the angle. With a defiant grin, he braced against a basalt outcropping and hurled the heavy induction coil down toward the scout, knowing Kaio would catch it.
